back: The C–OH carbon is bonded to one, two or three other carbon atoms respectively.
Steam, H₃PO₄ catalyst on silica, about 300 °C and 60-70 atm; unreacted ethene recycled.

front: Why alcohols boil higher than alkanes of similar Mr
back: Hydrogen bonds form between –OH groups (δ+ H to a lone pair on O) of neighbouring molecules.
Small alcohols mix completely (–OH hydrogen bonds with water); solubility falls as the hydrocarbon chain lengthens.

front: Effect of branching on alcohol boiling points
back: Branched isomers are more compact: less surface contact, weaker dispersion forces, lower boiling point.
Fermentation: renewable, low energy, batch, dilute product. Hydration: crude-oil based, continuous, fast, pure, 100% atom economy.

front: Acidity of ethanol compared with water
back: Ethanol is weaker: the electron-donating ethyl group destabilises C₂H₅O⁻ compared with OH⁻.

front: Why fermentation stops at about 15% ethanol
back: The ethanol concentration becomes toxic to the yeast, killing it.
